lesson.title: Functions with 2D Data
lesson.driving_question: How can functions reuse operations on a shared record structure?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Passing 2D-list data into functions that display and search records
lesson.concept_budget: Pass a 2D list as an argument to display and search functions using already-taught syntax.
misconceptions: A parameter can receive a complete 2D list.
The function traverses the argument supplied by the caller.
Search results should be returned or displayed consistently.
The main program should coordinate rather than duplicate row logic.
lesson.progression_note: Integrates the two Grade 8 strands immediately before the recap-style capstone.

primm.prompt: Recall how a parameter receives an argument, how a loop visits each row, and how return sends one value to the caller.
Use chess. Trace the function call, the row that matches, and the value stored in members.
Run with chess and then music. Confirm the search function returns 18 for a match and -1 after no match.

questions: What value is passed into records when find_members(clubs, name) runs?
Why must return -1 come after every row has been checked?
What happens if the target is not normalised in the same way as stored record names?
How does returning a field value differ from printing it inside the function?

primm.prompt: Use find_members() twice: once with "art" and once with "code". Store both returned values and display "Art: 12" and "Code: 15" after the three club names.
Add a function total_members(records) that loops through the rows, maintains a running total, and returns it. Display the labelled total; the supplied data must produce 45.

Store ["ari", 7], ["bao", 9] and ["cleo", 8] in [results]. Write show_records(records) to display every name and score. Write find_score(records, target) to return the matching score or -1. Write highest_score(records) to return the highest score. In the main program, call all three functions. Test "Bao"; display "Score: 9" and "Highest score: 9". Test "Mina"; display "Name not found." and "Highest score: 9".
Repair the missing data argument, row indexing and return placement so the search works for every row.
